title: Mumbai PM2.5 Analysis (2023–2025)
code: if (!require("pacman")) {   install.packages("pacman") } #  Load packages pacman::p_load(   vayuayan,   tidyverse,   tidylog,   terra,   sf,   tidyterra,   gstat,   ggview,   gstat,   sp,   exactextractr ) # Get Delhi Ground Data (CPCB) delhi_ground <- cpcb_download_city_data(   city = "Delhi",   year = 2023,   "delhi_aqi_2023.csv" )  # Load the wide data delhi_wide <- read.csv("delhi_aqi_2023.csv")  # Reshape from Wide to Long delhi_ground <- delhi_wide %>%   # Remove the 'Day' column and pivot all months   pivot_longer(     cols = -Day,     names_to = "Month_Name",     values_to = "ground_pm25"   ) %>%   # Convert month names to numbers (January -> 1, etc.)   mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%   # Remove any NAs (like Feb 30th) and aggregate to monthly mean   filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%   group_by(month) %>%   summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(ground_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")  print(delhi_ground) # Extract the 12 months delhi_sat_results <- lapply(1:12, function(m) {   message(paste("Processing Month:", m))   delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan")   stats <- pm25_get_stats(     geojson_file = delhi_geojson,     year = 2023,     month = m   )   data.frame(month = m, sat_pm25 = stats$mean) })  # Combine into satellite dataframe delhi_sat_df <- do.call(rbind, delhi_sat_results)  # Check results print(delhi_sat_df) # Join the ground spikes with the new satellite spikes delhi_final <- delhi_ground %>%   inner_join(delhi_sat_df, by = "month")

code: delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan") delhi_districts <- st_read(delhi_geojson)  # Load the Satellite Raster (e.g., Nov 2023) nov_raster <- rast("pm25_data/V6GL02.04.CNNPM25.GL.202311-202311.nc")  # Zonal Statistics: Get average PM2.5 per district # Step to turn a heatmap into a choropleth district_means <- terra::extract(   nov_raster,   vect(delhi_districts),   fun = mean,   na.rm = TRUE )  # Join the data back to the shapes delhi_districts$sat_pm25 <- district_means[, 2] ggplot() +   # Choropleth layer   geom_sf(     data = delhi_districts,     aes(fill = sat_pm25),     color = "white",     linewidth = 0.3   ) +   # Ground Stations (All 40)   geom_sf(     data = delhi_full_sf,     color = "royalblue4",     size = 2.5,     alpha = 0.65   ) +   scale_fill_distiller(     palette = "Spectral",     direction = -1   ) +   labs(     title = "Delhi District-Wise PM2.5 Choropleth",     subtitle = "District colors = Satellite Average | Red dots = CPCB Station Locations",     caption = "Do districts with more dots show better ground-satellite alignment?"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   ggview::canvas(width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

title: Delhi PM2.5 Analysis (2023)
text: Particulate matter smaller 2.5 micrometres (PM2.5) one harmful air pollutants — small enough enter bloodstream cause cardiovascular respiratory disease. Delhi consistently ranks among polluted cities world, winter months (October–January) seeing PM2.5 concentrations far exceeding safe limits. vignette demonstrates vayuayan package can used combine two independent data sources — satellite-derived PM2.5 estimates Washington University (WUSTL ACAG) ground-level CPCB monitoring station readings — analyse Delhi’s air quality 2023. also investigate critical policy question: existing 40 CPCB monitoring stations distributed well enough capture full spatial extent pollution, -monitored regions PM2.5 systematically missed?

title: Delhi PM2.5 Analysis (2023)
text: Monthly PM2.5 estimates sourced Washington University St. Louis Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group (WUSTL ACAG) V6.GL.02.04 product. dataset provides gridded PM2.5 concentrations approximately 0.01° resolution (~1km), derived combination satellite aerosol optical depth retrievals, chemical transport modelling, ground-based calibration. Files downloaded NetCDF (.nc) format using pm25_download_netcdf() function vayuayan.

what: 1. Seasonal trend: ground vs satellite PM2.5
title: Delhi PM2.5 Analysis (2023)
text: Note: 2024 2025, ground data available satellite component pending official NetCDF release Washington University.
code: # Get Delhi city-level ground data delhi_ground <- cpcb_download_city_data(   city          = "Delhi",   year          = 2023,   save_location = "delhi_aqi_2023.csv" )  # Load and reshape wide → long delhi_wide <- read.csv("delhi_aqi_2023.csv")  delhi_ground <- delhi_wide %>%   pivot_longer(     cols      = -Day,     names_to  = "Month_Name",     values_to = "ground_pm25"   ) %>%   mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%   filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%   group_by(month) %>%   summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(ground_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")  print(delhi_ground) delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan")  delhi_sat_results <- lapply(1:12, function(m) {   stats <- pm25_get_stats(     geojson_file = delhi_geojson,     year         = 2023,     month        = m   )   data.frame(month = m, sat_pm25 = stats$mean) })  delhi_sat_df <- do.call(rbind, delhi_sat_results) delhi_final <- inner_join(delhi_ground, delhi_sat_df, by = "month")  print(delhi_final) ggplot(delhi_final, aes(x = month)) +   geom_line(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), linewidth = 1) +   geom_line(     aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite (Monthly)"),     linewidth = 1,     linetype = "dashed"   ) +   geom_point(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), size = 2) +   geom_point(aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite (Monthly)"), size = 2) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +   scale_color_manual(values = c(     "CPCB Ground"               = "#d77027ff",     "WUSTL Satellite (Monthly)" = "#4575b4"   )) +   labs(     title = "Delhi 2023: PM2.5 Satellite vs CPCB Ground Estimates",     y     = expression(paste("PM2.5 Concentration (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")")),     x     = NULL,     color = NULL   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

text: November represents peak pollution season Delhi due crop burning, Diwali firecrackers, temperature inversion trapping pollutants near surface.
code: delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan") delhi_shape <- st_read(delhi_geojson, quiet = TRUE) nov_raster <- rast("pm25_data/V6GL02.04.CNNPM25.GL.202311-202311.nc") delhi_raster <- crop(nov_raster, vect(delhi_shape)) delhi_raster_mask <- mask(delhi_raster, vect(delhi_shape))  ggplot() +   geom_spatraster(data = delhi_raster_mask) +   geom_sf(     data      = delhi_shape,     fill      = NA,     color     = "royalblue4",     linewidth = 0.65   ) +   scale_fill_whitebox_c(     palette = "muted",     name    = expression(paste("PM2.5 (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")"))   ) +   labs(     title    = "Spatial Distribution of PM2.5 in Delhi",     subtitle = "Satellite Estimate: November 2023",     caption  = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V6.GL.02.04"   ) +   theme_minimal()

code: # Get station list delhi_station_list <- cpcb_get_station_list("Delhi")  # Add coordinates via OpenStreetMap geocoding # Cached to CSV to avoid re-geocoding on every render (~40 seconds) if (file.exists("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv")) {   delhi_station_list <- read.csv("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv") } else {   delhi_station_list <- cpcb_add_coords(delhi_station_list)   write.csv(delhi_station_list, "delhi_stations_with_coords.csv", row.names = FALSE) }  delhi_full_sf <- st_as_sf(   delhi_station_list,   coords = c("lon", "lat"),   crs    = 4326 )  print(delhi_station_list[, c("value", "label", "lat", "lon")]) delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan") delhi_districts <- st_read(delhi_geojson, quiet = TRUE) nov_raster <- rast("pm25_data/V6GL02.04.CNNPM25.GL.202311-202311.nc")  district_means <- terra::extract(nov_raster, vect(delhi_districts),   fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE ) delhi_districts$sat_pm25 <- district_means[, 2]  ggplot() +   geom_sf(     data      = delhi_districts,     aes(fill = sat_pm25),     color     = "white",     linewidth = 0.3   ) +   geom_sf(     data  = delhi_full_sf,     color = "royalblue4",     size  = 2.5,     alpha = 0.65   ) +   scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Spectral", direction = -1) +   labs(     title    = "Delhi District-Wise PM2.5 Choropleth",     subtitle = "District colors = Satellite Average | Blue dots = CPCB Station Locations",     caption  = "Do districts with more dots show better ground-satellite alignment?"   ) +   theme_minimal()

what: 4. Monitoring gap analysis: where are sensors missing pollution?
title: Delhi PM2.5 Analysis (2023)
text: key limitation ground-based monitoring spatial coverage. 40 CPCB stations uniformly distributed across Delhi — districts multiple stations others none. raises important policy question: districts sensors, satellite data suggest pollution levels underestimated? answer , interpolate ground PM2.5 readings across Delhi using Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) — fast spatial interpolation method estimates values unsampled locations based nearby station readings. delta (satellite − IDW ground) reveals sensor network may missing pollution.
code:
# Download winter (Oct-Jan) per-station PM2.5 if (!dir.exists("station_data")) dir.create("station_data")  station_raw <- lapply(seq_along(delhi_station_list$value), function(i) {   id <- delhi_station_list$value[i]   file <- paste0("station_data/", id, ".csv")    tryCatch(     {       if (!file.exists(file)) {         cpcb_download_station_data(           station_id    = id,           year          = 2023,           save_location = file         )       }       df <- read.csv(file)        df %>%         pivot_longer(cols = -Day, names_to = "Month_Name", values_to = "pm25") %>%         mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%         filter(month %in% c(1, 10, 11, 12), !is.na(pm25)) %>%         summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%         mutate(value = id)     },     error = function(e) {       data.frame(value = id, ground_pm25 = NA)     }   ) })  station_ground <- do.call(rbind, station_raw)  # Join with coords station_ground_sf <- station_ground %>%   filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%   left_join(     delhi_station_list %>% select(value, lat, lon),     by = "value"   ) %>%   filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) %>%   st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)  cat(nrow(station_ground_sf), "stations with valid winter PM2.5
") # Build winter average satellite raster (Oct-Jan) winter_rasters <- rast(lapply(c(1, 10, 11, 12), function(m) {   rast(sprintf("pm25_data/V6GL02.04.CNNPM25.GL.2023%02d-2023%02d.nc", m, m)) })) winter_raster <- mean(winter_rasters)  delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan") delhi_shape_union <- st_read(delhi_geojson, quiet = TRUE) %>%   st_union() winter_delhi <- crop(winter_raster, vect(delhi_shape_union)) winter_delhi <- mask(winter_delhi, vect(delhi_shape_union))  # District winter means for choropleth base delhi_districts$winter_sat_pm25 <- exact_extract(   winter_delhi, delhi_districts, "mean" ) # Project to UTM zone 43N for distance-based interpolation station_utm <- st_transform(station_ground_sf, crs = 32643) delhi_utm <- st_transform(st_as_sf(delhi_shape_union), crs = 32643)  # 1km prediction grid over Delhi bbox <- st_bbox(delhi_utm) grid_sf <- expand.grid(   x = seq(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"], by = 1000),   y = seq(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"], by = 1000) ) %>%   st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32643) %>%   st_filter(delhi_utm)  # IDW interpolation (idp=2: inverse square distance weighting) station_sp <- as(station_utm, "Spatial") grid_sp <- as(grid_sf, "Spatial") idw_out <- idw(ground_pm25 ~ 1, station_sp, grid_sp, idp = 2)  # Convert to raster idw_sf <- st_as_sf(idw_out) %>% st_transform(crs = 4326) idw_rast <- rasterize(vect(idw_sf), winter_delhi, field = "var1.pred") # Delta = satellite - IDW interpolated ground delta_rast <- winter_delhi - idw_rast delta_rast <- mask(delta_rast, vect(delhi_shape_union))  delta_df <- as.data.frame(delta_rast, xy = TRUE) %>%   rename(delta = 3) %>%   filter(!is.na(delta))  ggplot() +   # Base: district satellite PM2.5   geom_sf(     data      = delhi_districts,     aes(fill = winter_sat_pm25),     color     = "white",     linewidth = 0.2   ) +   # Delta overlay   geom_raster(     data  = delta_df,     aes(x = x, y = y, fill = delta),     alpha = 0.6   ) +   # CPCB station locations   geom_sf(     data  = station_ground_sf,     color = "black",     fill  = "yellow",     size  = 3,     shape = 21,     alpha = 0.95   ) +   scale_fill_gradient2(     low      = "#2166ac",     mid      = "#f7f7f7",     high     = "#d6604d",     midpoint = 0,     name     = expression(paste(Delta ~ PM[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))   ) +   labs(     title    = "Delhi Winter 2023: Where Are Sensors Missing Pollution?",     subtitle = "Red = satellite sees more pollution than ground sensors capture
Blue = sensors overestimate | Yellow = CPCB station locations",     caption  = "Delta = satellite − IDW interpolated ground | Winter avg Oct–Jan 2023
Source: WUSTL ACAG V6.GL.02.04 + CPCB CAAQMS"   ) +   coord_sf() +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(     plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),     plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40"),     legend.position = "right"   )

title: Delhi PM2.5 Analysis (2023)
text: seasonal trend analysis confirms Delhi’s well-documented pollution pattern — PM2.5 peaks sharply November–January driven crop residue burning neighbouring states, temperature inversions, reduced wind speeds. Satellite ground estimates broadly agree seasonality, though ground readings consistently higher satellite estimates, likely due point--area comparison caveat noted Methods section. spatial heatmap (November 2023) reveals pollution uniform across Delhi — northwestern outer districts tend show elevated PM2.5 relative central areas, though variation exists fine spatial scales 40-station network may fully capture. monitoring gap analysis (delta map) provides policy-relevant finding: districts shown red satellite-estimated PM2.5 significantly higher nearest ground station records. regions existing monitoring network may providing incomplete picture actual population exposure — necessarily air cleaner , sensors sparse. finding can inform decisions new CAAQMS stations prioritised.

title: vayuayanR - Air Quality Data Analysis for India
text: vayuayan R package fetching analyzing air quality data multiple sources: WUSTL ACAG: Washington University satellite PM2.5 data (Global) CPCB India: Central Pollution Control Board monitoring network (India ) R port Python package vayuayan. ## Etymology Vayuayan (वायुअयन) combines two Sanskrit words: - Vayu (वायु): Wind, air - Ayan (अयन): Path, journey, movement Together, “Vayuayan” means “path wind” - representing journey movement air quality data across space time.

title: vayuayanR - Air Quality Data Analysis for India

code: # Install devtools install.packages("devtools")  # Install vayuayan devtools::install_github("saketlab/vayuayan-r")

code: # Load package library(vayuayan)  # Create historical data client historical <- CPCBHistorical$new()  # Get list of states states <- historical$get_state_list() print(states)  # Get cities in Maharashtra cities <- historical$get_city_list("Maharashtra") print(cities)  # Get stations in Mumbai stations <- historical$get_station_list("Mumbai") print(stations)  # Download city-level data historical$download_city_data(   city = "Mumbai",   year = 2024,   save_location = "mumbai_aqi_2024.csv" )  # Download station-level data historical$download_station_data(   station_id = "site_5964",   year = 2024,   save_location = "station_data_2024.csv" )

title: vayuayanR - Air Quality Data Analysis for India
code: # Create live monitoring client live <- CPCBLive$new()  # Get your current location (IP-based) location <- live$get_system_location() print(location)  # Find nearest monitoring station nearest <- live$get_nearest_station() print(nearest)  # Get live AQI data for nearest station aqi_data <- live$get_live_aqi_data() print(aqi_data$metrics)  # Get live AQI for specific coordinates aqi_data <- live$get_live_aqi_data(   coords = c(19.0760, 72.8777)  # Mumbai coordinates )  # Get live AQI for specific station and time aqi_data <- live$get_live_aqi_data(   station_id = "site_5964",   date = "2024-02-25",   hour = 10 )

title: vayuayanR - Air Quality Data Analysis for India
code: # Create PM2.5 client pm25 <- PM25Client$new(cache_dir = "pm25_cache")  # Get PM2.5 statistics for a region (combines all polygons) delhi_stats <- pm25$get_pm25_stats(   geojson_file = "delhi_ncr.geojson",   year = 2023,   month = 11 ) print(delhi_stats)  # Get PM2.5 statistics grouped by state state_stats <- pm25$get_pm25_stats(   geojson_file = "india_districts.geojson",   year = 2023,   month = 11,   group_by = "state_name" ) print(state_stats)  # Get PM2.5 statistics grouped by multiple columns district_stats <- pm25$get_pm25_stats(   geojson_file = "india_districts.geojson",   year = 2023,   month = 11,   group_by = "state_name,district_name" ) print(district_stats)  # List cached NetCDF files pm25$list_cached_files()  # Clear cache pm25$clear_cache()
